concerns.text: Leftover editing artifact after scenario 1: "The specific value to remove/generalize: 'k' / Rewritten passage:." — this is dangling revision scaffolding, not a requirement statement, and corrupts the US-2 acceptance scenario text. Remove it.

Two of three Edge Cases have no backing FR/SC: (a) undefined stereochemistry in SMILES ("normalize or flag, not crash") and (b) highly flexible molecules where 2D descriptors may fail ("error analysis should highlight these outliers") are stated goals with no FR or SC. Only the NaN case is covered (FR-006). Add FRs/SCs for stereochemistry handling and flexible-molecule outlier analysis, or explicitly descope them.

Corrupted leftover editing artifacts inside the scenario: 'The specific value to remove/generalize: 'k'' and 'Rewritten passage:.' appear mid-requirement, truncating the R²/500-iterations acceptance clause. This is broken prose that makes the scenario unparseable.

FR-001 mandates 'a feature matrix of ≥200 2D topological descriptors', while FR-007 mandates iteratively removing the highest-VIF feature until all VIF ≤ 5.0. VIF pruning on a 200+ descriptor set will almost certainly remove many features, so the two FRs can be simultaneously unsatisfiable. Clarify whether the ≥200 floor applies pre- or post-collinearity pruning.

Undefined term 'the generated D descriptors' — 'D' is never defined anywhere in the spec; elsewhere the same concept is called '2D descriptors' / '2D topological descriptors'. Terminology should be stable.
SC-003 says 'Jaccard similarity of the top SHAP features' while FR-005 and US-3 specify 'top 10 SHAP features'. Align the wording (state 'top 10' in SC-003) so the measured quantity is unambiguous.

Leftover editing artifact embedded in the spec: "The specific value to remove/generalize: 'k' / Rewritten passage:." This corrupts the acceptance scenario and makes FR-002's test procedure ambiguous. Remove the artifact and state the scenario cleanly.

"peak memory usage remains within acceptable limits for standard deployment environments" is unmeasurable as written. SC-004 already fixes ≤6 GB / ≤6 h on a GitHub Actions runner — reuse that concrete reference here so the scenario is checkable.
"strictly under a predetermined threshold" names no threshold or reference. Point it at the constitution's ≤6 GB limit (as SC-004 does) so the requirement is verifiable rather than self-referential.

"molecules in QM9 that are known to be highly flexible" — no criterion for identifying flexibility (e.g., rotatable-bond count) is given, so "error analysis should highlight these specific outliers" cannot be checked. Specify a deterministic flexibility proxy or a documented selection procedure.

"the model converges within 500 iterations" — LightGBM does not report convergence; specify the checkable form (e.g., training completes with num_iterations ≤ 500, or early-stopping round count logged) so the scenario is deterministically verifiable.

Under-reach: the idea's methodology explicitly requires a 'Baseline Comparison: Compare the 2D-only model performance against a theoretical baseline that assumes no 3D information is available, quantifying the performance gap (if any) attributable to the lack of conformational data.' The spec's only baseline (SC-001, US-2) is a null mean-predictor model, which does not quantify the gap attributable to missing 3D/conformational information. Add an FR/SC for this comparison or explicitly justify its absence.

Under-reach: the idea's expected results center on performance degradation 'for flexible or highly polarizable systems where 3D conformation is critical.' The spec mentions flexible molecules only as an Edge Case ('error analysis should highlight these specific outliers') with no corresponding FR or SC requiring a rigid-vs-flexible error analysis. Promote this to a requirement so the hypothesis is actually testable.

Corrupted leftover editing artifact: '...on the k-fold cross-validation The specific value to remove/generalize: 'k' Rewritten passage:.' This garbled text breaks the scenario statement; rewrite the scenario cleanly.

The idea's preprocessing sketch lists 'topological polar surface area' among the 2D descriptors; the spec excludes TPSA/TPSA_E as target-redundant proxies. Excluding a target-correlated feature is defensible methodological rigor, but the spec should briefly justify why TPSA (a 2D descriptor, not 3D leakage) is excluded, so the exclusion is not read as silently narrowing the idea's descriptor set.

The research question is 'how much predictive information is captured by 2D versus 3D representations', yet the spec contains NO 3D or electronic baseline model. SC-001 validates the 2D model only against a null mean-predictor, which any non-trivial model beats. Without a 3D-conformer or charge-based comparison arm, the spec cannot answer its own central question; the 2D-vs-3D claim is untestable as designed.

FR-001(c) excludes 'any feature with |r| > 0.85 with the target dipole moment'. This conflates leakage with legitimate signal: a 2D descriptor strongly correlating with dipole moment is exactly the finding the research seeks, not contamination. Applying it also biases the answer toward '2D carries little information'. If retained, the correlation must be computed on the training split only — as written it leaks test-set target information into feature selection.

SC-002 measures the 'strongest signal' features 'against the SHAP value magnitude'. SHAP values quantify what the trained model relies on, not ground-truth feature importance; using the model's own attributions as the validation of which features 'carry the strongest signal' is partially circular. Add an independent check (e.g., single-feature predictive power or ablation performance drop) to corroborate SHAP rankings.

Scenario 1 is corrupted mid-sentence: '...on the k-fold cross-validation The specific value to remove/generalize: 'k' Rewritten passage:.' — leftover editing artifacts truncate the acceptance criterion and leave the R² threshold undefined.

FR-001 mandates ≥200 descriptors while FR-007 iteratively removes features with VIF > 5.0; on RDKit 2D descriptor sets (many near-collinear counts/indices) this can prune far below 200, silently changing the feature matrix the ≥200 requirement guarantees. State which requirement dominates or a floor for retained features.

new_concerns.text: NEW CONCERN — SCOPE DRIFT: FR-008 requires training a 3D-descriptor model ('radius-weighted atom-pair counts'), but Constitution VI (2D-Topological Fidelity) states 'All predictive models MUST rely exclusively on 2D molecular descriptors…any model utilizing 3D geometry or quantum-mechanical inputs violates the core scope.' A 3D-descriptor model directly violates this constitution principle. Either (a) remove FR-008 and SC-006 (revert to null-model baseline only), or (b) amend Constitution VI to permit a 3D baseline for comparison purposes with explicit scope boundary language. Current state is internally contradictory.

SC-003 and FR-005 require Jaccard similarity ≥ 0.7 for top-10 SHAP features across bootstrap resamples. This is a FIXED threshold on an empirical outcome. If the true stability is 0.65, the criterion fails even though the features are reasonably stable. Reframe as: 'report the Jaccard similarity of top-10 SHAP features across [deferred] bootstrap resamples; similarity ≥ 0.7 indicates high stability, 0.5–0.7 indicates moderate stability, < 0.5 indicates instability.' This converts a binary gate into a diagnostic metric.

Assumption states 'The dataset variables (predictors and outcomes) are fully contained within the QM9 release; no external data sources are needed for the 2D descriptors.' This is true but does not address whether QM9's dipole moments are calculated consistently (same QM method, basis set, etc.). Add: 'QM9 dipole moments are calculated using a consistent quantum mechanical method (e.g., B3LYP/6-31G*), ensuring homogeneity of the target variable.'
